methodology:
Adecoagro is broken into 8 country × business-segment rows, refined from the previous 5-row aggregation. Argentine pampas now split into Buenos Aires (premium), Córdoba, and Santa Fe + La Pampa to reflect the Class-A vs. mid-tier pricing differential within Argentine pampas. Brazilian sugarcane split between MS and MG mill clusters.

Total ~519K acres of OWNED farmland across:
- Argentina cropping: 250K acres (BA 110K + Cordoba 75K + Santa Fe/LP 65K)
- Argentina rice: 60K acres (Entre Ríos with integrated mill)
- Argentina dairy: 36K acres
- Uruguay cropland: 141K acres
- Brazil sugarcane (owned base): 32K acres (~13K hectares; 200K+ ha managed total)

Per-segment FMV anchors, all 2024-2025 dated:
- Buenos Aires pampas: $5,200/acre — top of CREA + Compania Argentina de Tierras 2024 range
- Cordoba pampas: $4,800/acre — slight inland discount
- Santa Fe + La Pampa: $4,200/acre — mid-tier diversified cropping
- Entre Ríos rice: $3,200/acre — specialty discount
- Uruguay (Soriano/Colonia/Rio Negro): $5,500/acre — dollarized stability premium
- Brazilian sugarcane: $5,500/acre — mill-supply premium

Land book of $1,360M total reflects Net PP&E carve-out estimate. Adecoagro's full Net PP&E of $3,399M includes:
- 4 Brazilian sugar/ethanol mills (14M ton crushing capacity, depreciable)
- Argentine dairy processing facilities
- Rice mill in Entre Ríos
- Various irrigation and farm infrastructure

A more rigorous Adecoagro valuation would separately mark farmland at FMV (above), industrial mills at replacement cost or DCF, and dairy at going-concern multiples. The implied land-only NAV here is the farmland portion.

INDUSTRIAL CARVE-OUT (latest pass): Adecoagro's $3,399M total Net PP&E is now
explicitly split between farmland (8 land rows totaling $1,360M) and 4
industrial rows totaling $2,009M:
  • 4 sugar/ethanol/bioenergy mills (14M ton crush capacity)  — $1,400M
  • Argentine dairy facility (Free Stall + processing)         —   $200M
  • Rice mill (Entre Ríos)                                     —    $80M
  • Other infrastructure (irrigation, machinery, storage)      —   $329M

The industrial rows use excludeFromAcreTotals=true so they contribute to
total FMV and book but not to per-acre denominators on the land columns.
The acres column on each industrial row reflects unit count (mill count
or "1 facility") rather than acreage — flagged in fmvRationale on each row.

Industrial cap rates 8-13% reflect typical processing-asset operating
yields. Combined with the 4.5-6.5% farmland weighted range, the FMV-
weighted blended cap rate now reflects the multi-segment nature of
AGRO accurately.
